description: Use this when the user asks about reverse DNS, PTR records, or FCrDNS for a mail server IP. Check one sending IP's forward-confirmed reverse DNS (FCrDNS): reads the IP's PTR record, then resolves that hostname back and reports whether it returns to the same IP. `verdict` is confirmed (the pair agrees — what receivers want to see), ptr_missing (the IP publishes no reverse record), or mismatch (a PTR that does not resolve back). A PTR on its own proves nothing, because the IP's operator writes its own reverse zone — only the forward confirmation is evidence, so never report a bare PTR as verified. The fix is always made by whoever controls the IP (the hosting or mail provider), never in the sending domain's own DNS. Pass a public IPv4 or IPv6 address.

ip.description: The sending IP to check, IPv4 or IPv6. Must be a public address — private, loopback and CGNAT ranges have no meaningful reverse DNS and are refused.
ip.title: Ip
